name: BRONZE BUTER
affiliation_detail:
SecureWorks assessed "with moderate confidence" that BRONZE BUTLER "operates on behalf of China," based on Chinese characters in malware strings, documented links between the group's Daserf tool and the PRC-based NCPH hacking group, and a decrease in activity during PRC national holidays. (SecureWorks, 2017)
In April 2021, Japan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced that cyberattack  on Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) was "highly likely" conducted by Tick,  stating that "the Unit 61419 of the Chinese People's Liberation Army is behind"  the group. (MOFA JP, 2021; Recorded Future 2021)
Recorded Future's Insikt Group noted that TAG-74's (reportedly overlapping with Tonto Team, suspected affiliation to PLA) tool ReVBShell is "very likely" shared with Tick. (Recorded Future, 2023)
description:
BRONZE BUTER/Tick is a suspected Chinese cyber espionage group active since at least 2006, primarily focused on intellectual property and classified information from Japanese organizations. The group also targets entities in South Korea, and to a lesser extent Russia, Singapore, and Taiwan. (Symantec, 2016; Trend Micro, 2017; SecureWorks, 2017) In 2023, Japanese law enforcement attributed Tick to PLA Unit 61419,  a unit stationed in Qingdao, Shandong Province. (The Record, 2023)
SecureWorks' 2017 analysis documented the group's focus on "critical infrastructure, heavy industry, manufacturing, and international relations" in Japan, noting that "the diverse targeting suggests that the group may be tasked by multiple teams or organizations with varying priorities." (SecureWorks, 2017) The group is distinguished by its deep knowledge of Japan-specific software: it exploited a zero-day in the Japanese asset management product SKYSEA Client View in 2016, and in mid-2025 exploited another zero-day in the widely deployed Motex LANSCOPE Endpoint Manager. (SecureWorks/Sophos, 2025)
In 2019, Trend Micro documented Operation ENDTRADE, which targeted defense, aerospace, chemical, and satellite industries with multi-stage backdoors. (Trend Micro, 2019)
In 2021, ESET identified Tick as one of the first groups to exploit the ProxyLogon vulnerability in Microsoft Exchange, targeting a South Korean IT company before public patch availability. (ESET, 2021) Subsequently, Tick compromised an East Asian DLP software developer serving government and military clients, deploying the previously undocumented ShadowPy downloader and trojanizing legitimate installers that were transferred to two downstream customers via remote support tools. (ESET, 2023)
In 2021, Recorded Future’s Insikt Group has discovered procurement documents  that show the PLA Unit 61419 associated with Tick seeking "to purchase antivirus software from several major American, European, and Russian security companies," likely "as a testing environment for natively developed malware" or "to find previously undisclosed vulnerabilities." (Recorded Future, 2021)

campaigns.name: SKYSEA Client View Zero-Day Exploitation
campaigns.description: SecureWorks documented Tick exploiting a zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2016-7836) in SKYSEA Client View, a popular Japanese asset management product, from June 2016 through at least February 2019. The vulnerability allowed remote code execution on systems exposed to the internet. JPCERT/CC observed scanning activity exclusively targeting Japanese IP addresses.

campaigns.name: Operation ENDTRADE
campaigns.description: Trend Micro identified a campaign targeting defense, aerospace, chemical, and satellite industries — specifically organizations with head offices in Japan and subsidiaries in China. The group deployed new multi-stage backdoors and used compromised legitimate email accounts for malware delivery, targeting industries holding classified information.

campaigns.name: DLP Software Developer Supply Chain Compromise
campaigns.description: ESET documented Tick compromising an East Asian DLP software developer whose customer portfolio included government and military entities. Beginning March 2021, the group deployed Netboy, Ghostdown, and ShadowPy, then trojanized Q-Dir installers and compromised internal update servers. In February and June 2022, the malicious installers were transferred to two downstream customers (engineering and manufacturing firms) via remote support tools. Tick also exploited ProxyLogon to compromise a South Korean IT company around the same time.

campaigns.name: LANSCOPE Endpoint Manager Zero-Day Campaign
campaigns.description: SecureWorks/Sophos CTU observed BRONZE BUTLER exploiting CVE-2025-61932, a critical zero-day (CVSS 9.8) in Motex LANSCOPE Endpoint Manager — a platform deployed by one in four listed companies and one in three financial institutions in Japan. The group deployed an updated Gokcpdoor backdoor with multiplexed communications and the Havoc C2 framework. CISA added the CVE to the KEV catalog on October 22, 2025.
